title: Fishing and Hunting Workers
description: Hunt, trap, catch, or gather wild animals or aquatic animals and plants. May use nets, traps, or other equipment. May haul catch onto ship or other vessel.

tasks.text: Scrape fat, blubber, or flesh from skin sides of pelts with knives or hand scrapers.
Remove catches from fishing equipment and measure them to ensure compliance with legal size.
Patrol trap lines or nets to inspect settings, remove catch, and reset or relocate traps.
Locate fish, using fish-finding equipment.
Kill or stun trapped quarry, using clubs, poisons, guns, or drowning methods.
Select, bait, and set traps, and lay poison along trails, according to species, size, habits, and environs of birds or animals and reasons for trapping them.
Put fishing equipment into the water and anchor or tow equipment, according to the fishing method used.
Track animals by checking for signs such as droppings or destruction of vegetation.
Skin quarry, using knives, and stretch pelts on frames to be cured.
Connect accessories such as floats, weights, flags, lights, or markers to nets, lines, or traps.
Harvest marine life for human or animal consumption, using diving or dredging equipment, traps, barges, rods, reels, or tackle.
Attach nets, slings, hooks, blades, or lifting devices to cables, booms, hoists, or dredges.
Release quarry from traps or nets and transfer to cages.

clusters.label: Operating Vehicles, Mechanized Devices, or Equipment

tasks.text: Steer vessels and operate navigational instruments.
Interpret weather and vessel conditions to determine appropriate responses.
Travel on foot, by vehicle, or by equipment such as boats, snowmobiles, helicopters, snowshoes, or skis to reach hunting areas.
Compute positions and plot courses on charts to navigate vessels, using instruments such as compasses, sextants, and charts.
Transport fish to processing plants or to buyers.
Wash decks, conveyors, knives, and other equipment, using brushes, detergents, and water.
Load and unload vessel equipment and supplies, by hand or using hoisting equipment.
Maintain and repair trapping equipment.
Maintain engines, fishing gear, and other on-board equipment and perform minor repairs.
Obtain permission from landowners to hunt or trap on their land.
Obtain required approvals for using poisons or traps, and notify persons in areas where traps and poison are set.
Direct fishing or hunting operations, and supervise crew members.
Oversee the purchase of supplies, gear, and equipment.
Sort, pack, and store catch in holds with salt and ice.
Teach or guide individuals or groups unfamiliar with specific hunting methods or types of prey.
Participate in animal damage control, wildlife management, disease control, and research activities.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Equipment Maintenance
skills.def: Performing routine maintenance on equipment and determining when and what kind of maintenance is needed.

skills.name: Troubleshooting
skills.def: Determining causes of operating errors and deciding what to do about it.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Map creation software
skills.def: Software to place data or metadata on a map. May include surveying or engineering features. Examples: MaxSea TIMEZERO, P-Sea WindPlot, Signet Nobeltec Catch, Trimble MyTopo Terrain Navigator Pro.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: DeerDays, Strat-Tech Deer Hunting Expert, Winchester Ammunition Ballistics Calculator.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Catchlog Trading Catchlog, OLRAC Electronic Logbook Software Solution.

skills.name: Inventory management software
skills.def: Software to maintain the inventory of businesses including restaurants or retail shops. Examples: Inventory management systems.
